prod_vs_preprod.test_case_steps_type: declared as object (background/created_at/feature/id/order/step/result/etc.), actual is always an empty array [] on every row observed, including rows with step_count 1 through 13 — confirmed across baseline (100 rows), ASC/DESC sorted samples, and required[fields] samples
prod_vs_preprod.summary: The sort trap does NOT reproduce on production: sort_by=name-ASC sorts correctly (verified strict ascending order over a real 16k-row project) and sort_by=name-DESC also sorts correctly (strict descending) — so on prod's real dataset neither direction silently no-ops; the preprod disagreement looks like it was a preprod-only artifact (small pool, possibly a caching/index quirk) rather than a real defect in the sort implementation. Everything else preprod found as DRIFT does reproduce on prod: info.count correctly reflects the true project-wide total (16,261, matching the ~16,267 fixture) while test_cases stays page-sized (confirms count-vs-rows works correctly at scale, this is actually NOT a defect — count is right), required[fields] silently nulls out assignee/owner/automation_state even for unrelated fields, sort_by+required[fields] column mismatch 422s as documented, per_page is honoured for valid values, test_case_steps is declared as an object but always returns an empty array regardless of step_count (container-type mismatch reproduces exactly), field_name is present on the priority/automation_state sub-objects, comments_count is declared but never returned, and several undeclared fields (reviewers, review_status, automation_state, is_shared, estimated_duration_seconds, template_step_type/id/name, step_count, test_run_results_count, test_run_results_issues_count, test_case_dataset) are returned on every row without being in the schema.

notes: Production project_id=332537 (Demo Project 1, identifier PR-18723) confirmed against fixture: total ~16,267 cases; info.count returned 16261 consistently across all probes (small live delta, not a bug). case_type and status objects were null on every sampled row across all probes (a data characteristic of this project's sampled cases, not something this probe can attribute to an endpoint defect — field_name presence was verified instead on the non-null priority and automation_state objects, both of which include field_name). No folder-scoping parameter is exposed by this capability outside all_folders=true, so the folder-40231630-specific steps check was done via representative rows returned in the whole-project reads (several of which belong to folder 40231630) rather than a folder-isolated call; test_case_steps was empty [] on all of them regardless of step_count. No writes or mutations were performed; all calls were read-only GETs against the list_test_cases capability.
